Monthly: 984,820×15=14,772,300; one creative draft gives 15,724,395–16,068,915. Returned hours: [120−(20 assembling+30 reviewing)]×(15×12)/60=210/year; ×€19–20=€3,990–4,200 gross. Baseline, volume, rate and target attention are assumptions, not demonstrated savings. Approve four weeks: two leads, six retrospective projects, S0–S1, agency workspace, creative shadow. Before week 1, operator remeasures routing; management/operator validate subscription capacity/terms. Week-4 live use depends on retrospective targets: precision >80%, survival >70%, review <30 minutes, Greek quality and adoption. Exact release conditions and spending authority remain unclear.
missing: Pilot budget, spending ceiling, implementation/support effort and subscription cost; net benefit cannot be calculated.
A Greek-quality pass threshold and a clear distinction between week-4 release criteria and month-2 adoption targets.
An unequivocal mandatory stop rule and explicit approval gate for month-2 default rollout.
Measured review time and validation of the 50-minute attention target; the graded review was not timed.
confusions: “Stop rule, recommended: if weeks 2–3 miss the targets, week 4 does not go live.” Is this binding or merely proposed?
“Greek naturalness rated 1–5 with EL/EN edit comparison” gives a measurement method but no passing score.
“at least 3 further leads request onboarding in month 2” cannot determine whether week 4 may go live.

“Approve the four-week pilot: usage is measured in tokens, the cost of running it is not yet, and week 1 settles both.” Capacity and routing are elsewhere required before week 1, while no cost-estimation owner or approval ceiling is specified.
fixes: Change “Pilot effort and operating costs are still to be estimated.” to specify an estimation owner, deadline, spending ceiling and financial approval gate.
Change “Stop rule, recommended:” to state explicitly whether the rule is mandatory, and name the week-4 release decision owner.
Change “Greek naturalness rated 1–5 with EL/EN edit comparison” to include a passing threshold; separate week-4 criteria from month-2 adoption measures.
